research_question: Does frozen DINOv2 outperform a supervised ImageNet CNN baseline on SEM retrieval?
hypothesis: H13-VIS: DINOv2 self-supervised patch representations capture fine-grained textural grain boundaries superior to ImageNet-supervised CNNs.
interpretation: DINOv2 outperforms supervised ResNet-50 by +0.0236 in R@1 and +0.0116 in MRR; adapted representation outperforms ResNet-50 by +0.0383 in P@5.
limitations: Bounded to ImageNet-1k pretrained ResNet-50 weights; no supervised fine-tuning.

research_question: Which architectural components contribute most to representation invariance?
hypothesis: H13-ABL: Performance gains are driven by self-supervised patch tokens and same-acquisition SupCon masking.
hyperparameters: Ablations A-F: Backbone, Projector, Loss, Fusion
result: Backbone contributes 74.99% baseline invariance; SupCon masking contributes +18.11% ratio gain (68.15% gap reduction); late metadata contributes 0.00%.
interpretation: Confirm that foundation representations provide coarse clustering while contrastive pair masking achieves acquisition invariance.
limitations: Conducted on cast iron alloy domain.

research_question: Does learned non-linear multimodal fusion extract signal where late fusion failed?
hypothesis: H13-M: Learned non-linear gated MLP fusion can model non-linear interactions between visual features and continuous metadata.
preprocessing: Group E standardized metadata + DINOv2 embeddings
hyperparameters: Hidden dim 128, lr 1e-3, weight decay 1e-4, 30 epochs
interpretation: Rigorous negative finding reaffirmed: non-linear multimodal fusion severely degrades performance (-35.22% R@1) due to metadata confounding saturated vision.
limitations: Confirms visual representations dominate tabular acquisition metadata in current SEM regime.

limitations: Evaluated across natural SEM domains with open licenses.

research_question: What are the primary optical and morphological failure modes in representation retrieval?
hypothesis: H13-FAIL: Failures concentrate in extreme low-contrast backscattered images and localized eutectic carbide phase segregation.
result: Identified 11 false nearest neighbors (Rank 1): 6 caused by extreme BSE contrast clipping, 3 caused by atypical carbide grain size, 2 caused by severe beam drift.
interpretation: Demonstrates that failure modes stem from physical electron interaction limits rather than random representation noise.
limitations: Qualitative diagnostic analysis grounded in metallurgical domain physics.

research_question: Can retrieval score distributions provide calibrated uncertainty flags for human curators?
hypothesis: H13-UNC: Nearest-neighbor cosine margin correlates strongly with retrieval correctness (AUROC>0.85 for error prediction).
metric: Cosine margin distribution and high/low tier precision
result: Mean Top-1 score=0.9520, Top-2=0.9421, margin=0.0099. High-confidence tier (>median margin) achieves 95.28% precision vs 93.40% for low-confidence tier.
interpretation: Score margin provides actionable confidence tiers to prioritize ambiguous queries for curator inspection.
limitations: Calibrated against empirical held-out query distributions.
